stories.title: Democrats vow to rein in Trump after midterm victory
stories.summary: Democrats have vowed to use their resounding midterm victory to rein in US President Donald Trump, setting up two years of possible deadlock in Washington, as Mr Trump spent his first post-election appearance showing off his under-construction White House ballroom. A wave of anger over Mr Trump's policies, particularly the US-Iran war's role in pushing the cost of living higher, helped Democrats take the Senate, where they flipped seats in deeply Republican states for a majority of at least 54 to 44. Democrats also gained at least 30 seats in the House of Representatives. It will be the first time that Mr Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with a Democratic-controlled Congress in both chambers. House of Representatives Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said the incoming majority will be focused on affordability and accountability. "We don't work for Donald Trump," said Mr Jeffries, a New York politician who is on track to become the first black speaker of the House.

stories.title: The races that will decide control of the US Senate
stories.summary: Democrats have an unexpected opportunity to seize control of the US Senate, with key races across several battleground states. Republicans hold a 53-47 majority in the Senate, where Democrats would need to flip at least two seats in states that US President Donald Trump carried by double digits in 2024 to win a majority in the midterm elections. As election day arrives, Democrats have a real chance at flipping the chamber, something that was considered a long shot at the beginning of this political cycle. Here are the races that will determine control of the Senate. Democrats' top priority is to hold the seats they already have. That means protecting US Senator Jon Ossoff in Georgia and helping progressive Abdul El-Sayed hold an open seat in Michigan. Donald Trump won Georgia by 2 percentage points in 2024 and Michigan by 1 point.

stories.title: Cross-border manufacturing event taking place in Dundalk
stories.summary: A cross border advanced and sustainable manufacturing event is taking place in Dundalk today. The event, hosted by the Advanced Manufacturing Training Centre of Excellence, will see small businesses, industry leaders, researchers and policy makers meet to discuss the industry. It comes as Ireland's first apprentices in Robotics and Automation started their training in Dundalk last month. The new course, which is the first and only one of its kind in Ireland, is run by the Louth Meath Education and Training Board at the Advanced Manufacturing Training Centre of Excellence (AMTCE) in the Louth town. The first batch of apprentices include seven men and two women, some of whom have just recently completed the Leaving Certificate. Others have been in the workforce for many years and are upskilling or retraining to get the Level 6 qualification.

stories.title: Ireland's game has to grow in 'every area' - Farrell
stories.summary: If there is concern that Ireland are not where they need to be less than a year out from the World Cup, then at least there is some reassurance that Andy Farrell and his coaches know it. Three and a half months on from a humbling 40-21 defeat to New Zealand, Ireland return to action on Friday night as they welcome Argentina to Aviva Stadium, the first of four games this month for Farrell's side. The third of those, against South Africa at the Aviva, will tell us a lot about where Ireland currently stand in rugby's food chain, and will dictate who they play a week later in London, in the finals week for this new tournament. As things stand, Farrell is under no illusions about how Ireland are stacking up. "For what's coming in 12 months’ time, if we’re honest with ourselves, where we are right now, is that good enough to board the plane believing 100% that we’ve a chance to win the World Cup? I don’t think so," the head coach said yesterday. Four years ago, Ireland went into the World Cup as the No 1-ranked team, and continued towards a 17-match winning run where they had beaten each of the game's big guns.

stories.title: Galway Bay Murders is John Connors' 'most important' role
stories.summary: John Connors has described his character in The Galway Bay Murders, Detective Eddie McDonagh, as "the most important character I've played" and has credited his wife and fellow actor Danielle Magennis with pushing him to audition for the role. When the body of a young woman is discovered on a Conamara bog, visiting NYPD detective Lieutenant Nora Savage (Star Trek: Voyager's Kate Mulgrew) and Detective Eddie McDonagh (Connors) are paired for the investigation. A formidable partnership forms in a twist-filled mystery that also explores climate activism, Traveller culture, and grief. While the role of Nora was written specifically for Mulgrew by writer-creator Verling, Connors' casting as Eddie was more circuitous. "I would never have had this role if it wasn't for my wife who read it - I was an advisor [on the series] and that - and she was like, 'Why are you not playing this role?' And I was like, 'Yeah, actually, I don't know...' She said, 'Well, you should be fighting for this role!' I was like, 'This is a great role, isn't it?!' She made me fight for this role. "I was kind of half prideful, going, 'Hang on, I'm good enough! They should know!' Typical man's thing. This is what men do: we go to pride, the destruction of all men!"

stories.title: Irish burger spot named second best in the world
stories.summary: Bunsen Burger, a Dublin institution with a famously pared-down menu, has been listed as having the second-best burger in the world. The mouth-watering list of The World's 50 Greatest Burgers was curated by Big 7, a travel blog that rounds up the best food, drink and experiences around the globe. Ranking everything from classic American cheeseburgers to Japanese Wagyu creations, Scandinavian reindeer patties to trendy smash burgers, the list was deliciously extensive. In the end, the top spot went to Hamburger America in New York City, but Bunsen was hot on its heels. The publication praised the Dublin restaurant's focus on quality over quantity, noting the "famously stripped back" menu and focus on "freshly ground beef" Founded by cousins Tom and Finn in Dublin in 2013, the restaurant has made waves in recent years, opening locations across Dublin, Cork and Belfast.

The singer will perform two shows each in Belfast, Galway, Kilkenny, Limerick and Cork next May and June. Brooks will then perform at UPMC Nowlan Park in Kilkenny on Friday 4 and Saturday 5 June, followed by TUS Gaelic Grounds in Limerick on Friday 11 and Saturday 12 June. The final two concerts will take place at SuperValu Páirc Uí Chaoimh in Cork on Friday 18 and Saturday 19 June. Speaking about his Irish tour Brooks said: "This has been a dream of mine since the first time we played Ireland. Once you get a taste of how the Irish love music, you can't play there enough!"

stories.title: Next's quarterly sales beat guidance on overseas seas
stories.summary: Clothing retailer Next has today reported a better-than-expected 8.1% rise in third-quarter full-price sales, as strong international growth offset a weaker UK performance, and maintained its full-year profit guidance. Next said UK sales rose 2.0% in the 13 weeks to October 31 year-on-year, down from growth of 3.6% in the first half but in line with guidance. The UK accounts for about three quarters of Next's sales. The group said UK trading had been volatile, with unseasonably warm weather adversely affecting sales in September before trading picked up in October. Online international sales rose 32.2%, accelerating from growth of 23.9% in the first half. Next said all of the sales over-performance came from its international business, with the additional £5m profit from these sales offset by increased operational costs. The group kept its forecast for a year to end-January 2027 profit before tax of £1.255 billion, up from the £1.158 billion made in 2025/26.

stories.summary: Brian Maher has nearly seen it all at Derry City, but the vantage point of the substitutes bench at Aviva Stadium is not something he wants to add to the list. Injuries have restricted him to just seven league appearances. Tom Norcott joined the club on loan from Reading until the end of the season and has taken over as a number one, but Maher did play the final two matches of the campaign. It gives interim boss Mark Connolly a big decision on which goalkeeper gets the nod.

stories.title: Niall Horan fans warned of major travel disruption
stories.summary: Niall Horan's four Dublin concerts will go ahead as scheduled next week, but fans are being warned to expect significant travel disruption, including restrictions on Luas services to 3Arena. Doors will open at 6.30pm each evening, with the concerts scheduled to begin at 7pm. The restrictions are being introduced as Dublin prepares to host a European Political Community summit on Thursday 12 November, followed by an informal meeting of EU leaders on Friday 13 November. Both meetings will take place at the Convention Centre Dublin, close to 3Arena. Although the concert venue is outside the security cordon, fans have been advised to allow additional travel time and plan their journeys carefully. There will be no east-west traffic along North Wall Quay from 10 to 13 November, although vehicles will still be able to access 3Arena via Seville Place, Sheriff Street Upper, East Wall Road and the Tom Clarke Bridge.

stories.title: 18 places to learn a new hobby in Dublin
stories.summary: With winter well and truly on the way, it can be too easy to slip into a habit of scrolling on your phone instead of making the most of the few fine days. Finding a hobby can not only get you away from screens, but help you connect with new people and communities, and even discover something new about yourself. From half-day micro classes to intensive 10-week long workshops, here's our pick of some of the best places to pick up a new hobby. And of course, always check your local community centre, adult education centre and businesses for pop-up events and workshops throughout the year. If you've always wanted to learn to make your own jewellery, look no further. Located on Drury St, this cosy workshop runs a number of day courses. Choose from their silver ring forging class (€95pp), a gemstone laying class (€175pp) or even learn how to carve a ring from wax (€140). Materials are provided. Change Clothes is a community based clothing reuse hub that is committed to teaching visitors how to get the most out of their clothing. While it's popular for its swap shop, the team also run workshops on clothes alterations and repair, from hemming and mending, to creative embroidery and taking in or out your jeans. They also offer courses such as ones on machine sewing for €25 if you want to take your new skills home! Centrally located on South Anne Street, the School of Jewellery is practically a one-stop shop for immersing yourself in jewellery making. Founded in 2011 by Deirdre O'Donnell, a goldsmith and designer, and now led by Paul Coyne, students can learn everything from stone setting and enamelling, to gold plating (keum-boo). Enquire directly to learn more about prices per class.

stories.title: Poor wastewater management harming the environment - EPA
stories.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency has warned that poor management of wastewater treatment plants by Uisce Éireann is harming the environment. A new report found that in 2025, 55% of wastewater treatment plants in Ireland discharged wastewater that failed to meet EPA standards. The EPA's report - 'Urban Wastewater Treatment in 2025' - found that roughly half of failures were due to deficient infrastructure, while the other half were due to poor operation and maintenance. It found that "common problems include equipment breakdowns and inadequate procedures and training". "The number of sites affected by such issues remains far too high, with no significant improvement compared to 2024," the report said. "Operation and maintenance issues can and must be addressed by Uisce Éireann without delay," the report said.

stories.title: Toyota posts profit surge as hybrid sales shine
stories.summary: Toyota has today booked its first profit gain in six quarters and lifted its annual outlook by 15%, as robust demand for higher-margin hybrid vehicles and a weaker yen offset a slide in sales in China and the Middle East. The results, along with plans to return up to $89 billion to shareholders over five years, helped send Toyota's shares soaring in Tokyo trade. The world's largest carmaker has benefited from its focus on petrol-electric hybrids, even as it faces considerable headwinds in the form of competition from Chinese electric vehicle makers and surging fuel prices in the wake of the Iran war. Toyota said it now expects operating profit of 3.9 trillion yen ($24.6 billion) for the year ending March after posting a forecast-beating 34% climb in income for the July-September quarter. Unlike other traditional car companies that went all-in on electric vehicles and then had to write down billions of dollars in investment when demand for EVs weakened, Toyota has mainly focused on advancing the hybrid technology it popularised with the Prius decades ago. The strategy has been key to its ability to defend market share in its main market, the US, despite the threat from fast-moving Chinese EV makers elsewhere.

stories.title: How did supermarket fridges become a target for hackers?
stories.summary: Supermarket fridges and freezers became the targets of cyberattacks across Europe on Monday, with temperatures in units in some stores rising to as high as 50C. In Ireland, 13 SuperValu stores were affected, forcing chilled and frozen food to be removed from sale. Musgrave, the company behind SuperValu, said the incident was resolved that evening. The disruption came just weeks after hundreds of French supermarkets were hit by similar attacks, while cold storage rooms at some French blood banks were also targeted earlier this week. But how did equipment used to keep food cold become a target for hackers - and what do we know about how they got in? These controls allow engineers to check temperatures and change settings without visiting the shop. Danfoss controllers were also among the systems targeted by last month's cyberattack in France which caused refrigerators to overheat at around 700 supermarkets.

stories.title: Sony Q2 profit jumps on Spider-Man and PlayStation boost
stories.summary: Sony has today reported a 45% rise in second-quarter operating profit to 622.3 billion yen ($3.95 billion), beating market estimates, due to stronger performance at its games and movies units. Contributors to the stronger performance, which led the Japanese entertainment and technology conglomerate to hike its full-year profit outlook by 9%, included the hit movie "Spider-Man: Brand New Day". Sony's games business is expected to be a major beneficiary of the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI" on November 19 but is grappling with higher memory chip prices due to the AI boom. Companies continue to be squeezed by elevated memory prices, with iPhone maker Apple this week flagging pressure on margins over the Christmas quarter. The PlayStation maker said in July it had secured the amount of memory needed to meet its projected sales volume this year. During the second quarter, Sony sold 2.6 million PlayStation 5 units, compared to 4 million in the same period a year earlier.

stories.title: Drought chasing title glory after strong season in Spain
stories.summary: Tipperary driver Nicole Drought will travel to Circuito de Jerez in southern Spain this weekend for the season finale of the Spanish GTX AM Championship, aiming to finish her maiden international GT campaign on a high by clinching the title on her debut season. Driving the #75 Protech Motorsport Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 CS alongside co-driver Lucas Fothergill, Drought has established herself as a strong contender in the highly competitive GTX AM category during her first season of Iberian Supercars competition. The Jerez finale is the culmination of a season that has seen Drought make a transition onto the international GT racing stage in impressive style. Among the highlights was a superb double class victory at the famous Circuito del Jarama in June, where Drought and Fothergill combined front-running pace with consistent race management to take both GTX AM wins. More recently, the pairing secured a double podium at Valencia, finishing second and third in class across the weekend's two races. They currently lead the GTX AM Championship by just 11 points and they will race twice this weekend, once on Saturday and once on Sunday, with the championship being decided before Sunday evening.

stories.title: Councillors divided over private security plan for Dublin
stories.summary: Plans to examine the introduction of private security in Dublin city centre have divided city councillors. The Dublin City Development Company (DCDC), the body responsible for the area's regeneration, said it has been liaising with gardaí, the Department of Justice and businesses about the introduction of safety wardens, who would not have powers of arrest. While some councillors have said they are open to exploring the concept, others have expressed concerns about the proposals. In a statement, DCDC, which was established to implement the recommendations of the Government's Dublin City Taskforce, said it was tasked with developing agreements with business representative groups and gardaí for a new safety warden scheme. "Safety on our streets should be our number one priority. As part of recognising this deliverable, the Project Management Unit has been conducting research and looking to other jurisdictions to inform best practice on options to improve safety on our streets, implement change, and provide additional support to An Garda Síochána, residents and the business community. "Dublin City Council has been liaising with An Garda Síochána, the Department of Justice and the business community to develop concepts. We are also reviewing structures adopted by Irish Rail and Luas to understand the implementation of security measures on public transport.

stories.title: Govt should oppose aspects of UK Troubles Bill - cttee
stories.summary: The Government should formally oppose proposals requiring the Attorney General for England and Wales to give consent for Troubles-related prosecutions, an Oireachtas committee has said. Concerns have been raised that the amended Northern Ireland Troubles Bill, sent forward to the UK House of Lords two weeks ago, could undermine the independence of prosecutorial decision making. The Oireachtas Committee on Justice has completed pre-legislative scrutiny of the general scheme of the Government's legacy legislation. It is understood that its report recommends opposing the involvement of the Attorney General in such decisions, as well as any amendment that would remove provision for legacy inquests after the Legacy Commission is wound up. The Attorney General for England and Wales is a political appointee, with a separate Attorney General for Northern Ireland appointed by the First Minister and deputy First Minister under devolution. stories.title: Former F1 champion Alan Jones dies aged 80
stories.summary: Former Formula One world champion Alan Jones has died at the age of 80 following a brief illness. A statement from Jones' family, issued through Motorsport Australia, announced the death of the 1980 championship winner – who remains the last Australian to win the F1 title. Jones was only the second Australian to win the championship after Sir Jack Brabham, and topped the podium at 12 grands prix during a career that took in spells with Hesketh, Williams – with whom he won his title – and Arrows. "We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness," his wife Amanda Butler-Davis said. "He will be dearly missed and fondly remembered by those closest to him, as well as the many fans whose support he was always grateful for. "Alan dedicated his life to motorsport, building a legacy that will live on through the countless people he touched along the way.

stories.title: Rise in anti-social behaviour by girls over past decade
stories.summary: Anti-social behaviour has increased for girls and remained broadly stable for boys over the past decade, according to a new study. The research by the Economic and Social Research Institute shows an increase in the number of 13-year-old girls who reported hitting, punching or kicking someone. It found that the increase appears to relate to greater mental health difficulties - including depression, hearing voices and behavioural problems. The research also found that young people who become increasingly involved in anti-social behaviour during their teenage years are more likely to experience poorer educational outcomes and difficulties with their mental health and wellbeing in early adulthood. The study used data from the Growing Up in Ireland study to examine anti-social behaviour among young people between the ages of 13 and 17. Anti-social behaviour includes a range of activities, from taking something without permission and graffiti to physical violence.

stories.title: Moylan bags hat-trick but Cardiff blow three-goal lead
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland international Jack Moylan rattled home a brilliant hat-trick for Cardiff who squandered a three-goal lead to draw 3-3 at West Ham in a Championship thriller on Wednesday night. In what was new boss Scott Parker's first game in charge of the Hammers, Moylan stole the show in an incredible first half. The ex-Shelbourne man bagged his first hat-trick in English football to leave Brian Barry-Murphy's team in cruise control and Hammers fans venting their anger. But the hosts - inspired by captain Jarrod Bowen - fought back in remarkable fashion as Divine Mukasa, Arne Engels and Max Kilman netted to secure a point. Parker was confirmed as Hammers boss on Wednesday morning - just 24 hours after Nuno Espirito Santo's departure - but it was a tough watch for the former England midfielder initially as Moylan had Cardiff 3-0 ahead inside 39 minutes. Moylan scored a hat-trick on his Ireland debut against Grenada in May, but this was his first club treble since scoring three for Shels against Sligo Rovers in May 2023.

stories.title: Free period products initiative extended to all schools
stories.summary: Minister for Education Hildegarde Naughton is expected to announce the expansion of the free period products initiative to all eligible upper primary, post-primary and special schools from the 2027/28 school year. The announcement builds on the introduction of the initiative in DEIS Plus schools during the 2026/27 school year. The measure delivers on a key Programme for Government commitment to ensure that no student is held back in their education because of period poverty. Schools will receive annual grant funding from the Department of Education and Youth to provide free period products for students who may need them during the school day. The initiative follows consultation with students, teachers and school leaders, who expressed strong support for the provision of free period products in schools and highlighted concerns about rising costs and the impact of period poverty. Students who participated in the consultation emphasised the importance of being able to access period products discreetly, easily and without stigma while at school.

stories.title: Champions League wrap: Parrott starts as Betis are beaten
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland attacker Troy Parrott started for Real Betis as they took on Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League at the Westfalenstadion, but he was unable to prevent them falling to a 2-1 defeat. Konstantinos Karetsas struck a 72nd-minute winner as the German side handed Betis their first defeat of the campaign. Parrott started up front in a three-man attack and was lively from the off. It looked like he'd helped his side to an early lead when he led a counter-attack before squaring the ball for Antony to finish, but the offside flag went up. After a scoreless first half, Dortmund took control of the game when they hit the front four minutes after the restart. Jobe Bellingham's first-time shot from the a low cross was blocked, but Fabio Silva pounced on the rebound to put his side ahead. Betis drew level 20 minutes later when the 30-year-old Aitor Ruibal, who was making his first ever Champions League appearance, got on the end of a clever ball across the face of the goal from Abde Ezzalzouli and finished in style.

stories.title: Zelensky speaks to US envoys ahead of Russia talks
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he had a detailed conversation with US envoys ahead of several scheduled meetings between Ukrainian and Russian officials, starting with one at the White House to be hosted by US First Lady Melania Trump. The flurry of diplomacy comes as negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States prepare to meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November for the first talks between all three sides since February. The talks have revived hopes for peace, as Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine grinds through its fifth year, and a recent rapprochement between presidents Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin has raised concerns the US could turn its back on Ukraine. "We just had a very detailed, hour-and-a-half-long conversation with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner," Mr Zelensky said in a post on X yesterday evening, during a visit to Madrid. "The negotiations must move forward at full throttle to bring this war to an end as quickly as possible. Ukraine is ready to take the necessary steps," he said. His remarks came after Ms Trump's White House office said the US first lady would bring representatives of Russia and Ukraine together at the White House, without specifying a date.

stories.title: Irish rugby fans told to be wary of fake ticket platforms
stories.summary: Ireland rugby fans have been told to "exercise extreme caution" after a rise in reports of fake ticket sales for the Nations Championship and Six Nations. The IRFU said on Wednesday there had been a "significant increase" in cases of fraudulent sales ahead of the upcoming Tests against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa as well as the Six Nations showdowns with England and France. The only authorised sources for tickets are the Irish Rugby Account Manager platform through Ticketmaster, and Ticketmaster itself. Supporters who have made purchases tickets on unauthorised websites and ads - particularly those promoted through social media platforms - have later become aware they may have been scammed when receiving confirmation emails that lack key ticket information, e.g. the entry route and seating allocation. "We are seeing an increase in reports from supporters who have unknowingly purchased fraudulent digital tickets through websites and social media advertisements that appear legitimate at first glance," said IRFU director of communications Aoife Clarke. "Unfortunately, these sites can be highly convincing and often appear prominently through online advertising and social media channels. We are urging supporters to purchase tickets only through Ticketmaster or Ticketmaster's Irish Rugby Account Manager.

stories.title: Dozens missing after Russian strike on Ukraine aid centre
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian bombing of an aid distribution point in Ukraine's southeastern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday has risen to 37, with dozens missing, officials said, in one of the deadliest strikes on civilians this year. Rescuers were still searching for survivors in the rubble of the former school in the village of Komyshuvakha, a regional military administration spokesperson said. Ivan Fedorov, the co-head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Defence Council, wrote on Telegram that 59 people were missing. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Russian forces first dropped aerial bombs on the school building as people arrived to collect aid, then struck the shelter with more bombs. Classes have long since been suspended at the school because of its proximity to the front line, but it served as a shelter and handed out humanitarian aid every Monday, Mr Zelensky said. Two members of a rescue crew and four police officers were among the dead, emergency services said. Russia's Defence Ministry said the attack targeted Ukrainian military units around Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, and that up to 25 Ukrainian servicemen were killed.

stories.title: Musk jokes about election loss after spending record sums
stories.summary: Tech billionaire Elon Musk has joked about Republicans' defeat in US midterm elections after spending hundreds of millions of dollars to help the party. Democrats seized control of the US Congress last night, capturing both the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning rejection of President Donald Trump's political agenda. "Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn't work this time," Mr Musk said on X, including the shrug emoji. Mr Musk contributed nearly half a billion dollars to Republican political efforts, making him the largest individual contributor in a federal election cycle since unlimited election spending was allowed in 2010, according to campaign finance tracker OpenSecrets. His donations have mostly gone to his Republican-leaning America PAC, as well as to the Republican Senate Leadership Fund super PAC. The SLF used Musk's $158 million in donations in September to support Ken Paxton, the Republican Senate candidate in Texas.
